programs.title: Global Us
programs.desc: In Kishangarh, India, tourists flock to vast marble dumps despite hazardous dust pollution. Germany is deeply divided over the return of wolves. And off Brazil's coast, descendants search for a long-lost slave ship.

programs.title: DocFilm
programs.desc: A video diary from the frontline trenches: Ukrainian commander and cameraman Dmytro Dokunov can't save his comrades. Can he free himself from the horror of the Russian attack on Ukraine?

programs.title: Sports Life
programs.desc: After suffering two sudden cardiac deaths and a number of severe health complications, 32-year-old Tamara Schwab's life was saved by a heart transplant. She's now vowed not to waste a single minute of her second stint at life and is pushing herself to the limit to compete in the World Transplant Games. But can her body take it?

programs.title: Tomorrow Today
programs.desc: High-speed X-rays let researchers see exactly what happens during a collision. Also on the show: plastic-eating worms, a sailboat for ocean research, and why women in soccer run farther and play harder than men.

programs.title: DocFilm
programs.desc: Decades ago, gray seals in the Baltic Sea were considered virtually extinct, mercilessly hunted by humans. Thanks to a hunting ban, the population recovered. Now, they're making life difficult for fishermen.

programs.title: In Good Shape
programs.desc: Mouth ulcers, gum disease, cavities — even the tongue — can provide warnings of diabetes, heart disease, and stroke. Learn what your mouth says about health.

programs.title: HER Women in Asia
programs.desc: Reduce, reuse and recycle — to live a waste free life is the goal of more and more  people around the world. But where to start? HER introduces women with creative and innovative ideas on how to consume less and recycle more. And sometimes it's also, about showing that even waste can be turned into something wonderful.
